name: Cilium
summary: A Kubernetes networking and security system that attaches eBPF programs to node and endpoint paths, derives identity-aware policy, implements service load balancing, and exposes datapath observability.

features.name: eBPF endpoint datapath
features.description: Cilium uses eBPF programs attached at kernel networking hooks to process endpoint traffic and implement datapath behavior without requiring every decision in a user-space proxy.
features.benefits: Efficient, programmable packet processing close to the kernel path
features.costs: Kernel capabilities, verifier constraints, and program/map lifecycle become deployment dependencies

features.name: Identity-aware network policy
features.description: Cilium associates network policy with identities derived from endpoint labels and evaluates policy at datapath boundaries rather than relying only on IP addresses.
features.benefits: Policy can follow workload identity across endpoint address changes
features.costs: Identity allocation, policy distribution, and rule complexity affect correctness and scale

features.name: Service routing and datapath observability
features.description: Cilium implements Kubernetes service translation and load balancing in its datapath and provides observability around flows and policy decisions.
features.benefits: Integrates service routing, security, and flow visibility in one datapath
features.costs: Service state synchronization and high-volume telemetry add control and storage pressure

mathematical_views.question: How do endpoint hooks, eBPF programs, maps, and service backends transform packets?
assumptions: Hook points are graph vertices with ordered program transitions
Maps represent bounded shared datapath state
The view abstracts verifier and kernel scheduling details

mathematical_views.question: How do endpoint identities and policy rules determine allowed communication edges?
assumptions: Identity is modeled as a label-derived vertex attribute
Rules define allowed or denied relations between identities and ports
The view does not infer policy completeness from configured rules

mathematical_views.question: How does a Kubernetes service become a datapath load-balancing decision?
assumptions: Service and backend state are synchronized into datapath representations
A packet selects among currently eligible backends
The model does not claim availability during every update transition

benefits: Kernel-local programmable processing and fewer user-space hops
costs: Kernel/version constraints and verifier limits shape implementation
Identity distribution and policy evaluation add coordination state

benefits: Unified routing, enforcement, and flow visibility
costs: Datapath state and telemetry scale with endpoints and traffic
